project: The Arabic Tongue · Tier-A Indo-Iranian-sister cognates · Arabic ↔ Sanskrit

entries.notes: Shared core nucleus of binding/yoking two together.
entries.reading: z-w-j pair ↔ *yug- yoke: both = the joining-gesture; possible Nostratic, unproven

entries.notes: Cognate numeral: Arabic th-l-th maps to Sanskrit t-r-y.
entries.reading: three: Semitic θalāθ ↔ IE *trei — famous look-alike, not established cognate

entries.notes: Cognate numeral: s-t maps to Sanskrit s-s.
entries.reading: six: Semitic šdθ ↔ IE *sweḱs — famous look-alike

entries.notes: Cognate numeral: s-b-ʿ matches Sanskrit s-p-t.
entries.reading: seven: Semitic sabʿ ↔ IE *septm — famous look-alike

entries.notes: Reverent submission / law. n-m-s core.
entries.reading: Arabic ناموس is a GREEK loan (nomos "law"), not from Sanskrit namas — different etymology

entries.notes: Wanderwort: s-n-d-l matches c-n-d-n (c sounding like s/ts).
entries.reading: sandalwood — a trade Wanderwort that travelled the routes; a loan, not a cognate

entries.notes: Liquid/nasal swap: n-m matches s-m (with alif drop).
entries.reading: name: Semitic ism/šem ↔ IE *h1nomn — debated long-range

entries.notes: Liquid swap and pharyngealization.
entries.reading: أخ and bhrātṛ share no skeleton; bhrātṛ = English brother (IE), unrelated to أخ

entries.notes: Sanskrit bala (strength) maps to Arabic ba'l (lord/strength).
entries.reading: baʿl lord/might ↔ bala strength: convergent b-l power-gesture

entries.notes: Sanskrit root kṛ (to do/make) matches Arabic k-r (repetition/return).
entries.reading: كرّ repeat/charge ↔ kṛ do/make: the k-r action gesture, independently

entries.notes: Sanskrit makha (chief/head) matches Arabic m-ḫ (essence/brain).
entries.reading: مخّ marrow/brain ↔ makha: the m-ḫ inner-core gesture

entries.notes: Sanskrit las (shine/play/sound) matches Arabic l-s-n (tongue).
entries.reading: لسان tongue ↔ las shine/play: semantic bridge too loose

entries.notes: Bilabial nasal m- representing maternal gathered mass.
entries.reading: أمّ ↔ mātṛ: the UNIVERSAL م-mother baby-word (the universal floor) — convergence, not descent

entries.notes: Kinship source. Labial p- maps to b-, dental t- to t/d.
entries.reading: أب ↔ pitṛ: the universal father baby-word — convergence, not descent

entries.notes: Sibilant-dental transition (s/d) representing biting/gnashing.
entries.reading: سنّ (s-n) ↔ danta (IE *dent-): different roots; tooth-word coincidence

entries.notes: Nasal-guttural nucleus (n-kh) representing sharp point piercing.
entries.reading: نخس prod ↔ nakha nail/claw: the n-ḫ piercing-point gesture

entries.notes: Labial-dental nucleus (p-d) representing physical stamp/stride.
entries.reading: Arabic foot is قدم/رجل, not بد; pāda = IE *pod-; weak

entries.notes: Curved stop + rolling boundary (k-r-n) representing ear as horn/corner projection.
entries.reading: قرن horn ↔ karṇa ear/horn ↔ Lat cornu ↔ Eng horn: the famous k-r-n horn look-alike

entries.notes: Inward resonance + sibilant friction (n-s) representing respiration.
entries.reading: نسم breath/breeze ↔ nasa nose/breathe: the n-s breath gesture

entries.notes: Outer opening + settled fixity (v-d to b-d) representing manifest clarity.
entries.reading: بدا appear ↔ vid know/see (IE *weid-): the appear↔perceive link

entries.notes: Pharyngeal stop + binding loop (d-v to d-w) representing light.
entries.reading: ضوء light ↔ div sky/shine (IE *dyeu-): the famous day/sky look-alike (cf. our Tier-B ضحو↔dies)

entries.notes: Ignition stop + resonance emission (g-n to j-j) representing blazing flames.
entries.reading: أجّ blaze ↔ agni fire (Lat ignis): convergent fire-gesture

entries.notes: Dental contact + resonance (t-n) representing stretched tension.
entries.reading: طنّ resound/stretch ↔ tan stretch (IE *ten-): the t-n tension gesture

entries.notes: Rolling authority + closed assembly (r-j) representing the head/leader.
entries.reading: رجل man ↔ rāj king (IE *reg-, Lat rex): semantic stretch man↔king

entries.notes: Concentrated containment + resonance (m-n) representing mental measure.
entries.reading: منى/تمنّى wish ↔ man think (IE *men- mind): the m-n mind gesture, near-universal

entries.notes: Friction + dental stop (s-t to th-b-t) representing stable position.
entries.reading: ثبت be-firm ↔ sthā stand (IE *steh2-): the s-t standing-firm gesture

entries.notes: Bilabial container + glide (bh-u to b-y/w) representing existence/dwelling.
entries.reading: باء return/become ↔ bhū be/become (IE *bhuH-): the becoming gesture

entries.notes: Settled thrust + extension (d-a to d-y).
entries.reading: أدّى render ↔ dā give (IE *deh3-): the d-giving gesture, near-universal

entries.notes: Binding loop + movement glide (v-h to w-s/j).
entries.reading: وسق load ↔ vah carry (IE *wegh-, Lat vehere): the carrying gesture

entries.gloss: honey, sweet / to mix sweet drink
entries.notes: Gathered sweetness + dental slide (m-dh) representing honey/sweet drink.
entries.reading: مذق mix-drink ↔ madhu honey/mead (IE *medhu-, Eng mead): famous mead/madhu Wanderwort

entries.notes: Guttural-velar shift (ḥ to kh) + liquid-nasal swap (r to n) on identical excavation semantics.
entries.reading: حفر dig ↔ khan dig: NO skeleton overlap — pure back-throat-scrape=excavate gesture-parallel

entries.notes: Sibilant alignment (ṣ to s) + dental stop transition (d to t) + velar-glide slide (q to y) representing alignment with reality.
entries.reading: صدق truth ↔ satya true (IE sat- being/real): the s-t truth/being gesture

entries.notes: Palatal-velar stop transition (q to g) + labial shift (b to r/bh) + dental-guttural drift (ḍ to h) on identical grasping semantics.
entries.reading: قبض grasp ↔ grah seize (IE *ghrebh-): the q/g-r grasping gesture

note: IE FRONTIER — convergent parallels & Wanderwörter, NOT claimed genetic cognates. Per the framework, finding STRONG cognates in a distant family would be pareidolia; so there are ZERO PERFECT/STRONG here. Types: LONG-RANGE (famous deep look-alike, unproven) · WANDERWORT (trade loan) · CONVERGENT (independent same-gesture mapping) · COINCIDENCE (rejected on skeleton/semantics). This set tests the gradient: it MUST score low, and it does. Sources: Monier-Williams.
